description: Any object that replaces a real dependency in a test, whether it only feeds data or also records interactions.
A controllable replacement that supplies data to the code under test and is never the subject of an assertion.
A double the test asserts on, used when an interaction such as sending an email or publishing a message is the behavior being checked.
A small working implementation of an interface, such as an in-memory gateway, reused across tests instead of per-test library setup.
A point in the design, usually an injected interface or `TimeProvider`, where a test can substitute a dependency without changing production code.
Microsoft's `TimeProvider` subclass for tests whose clock only moves when the test calls `Advance` or `SetUtcNow`.
Since Xceed's 2025-01-13 announcement, commercial use of Fluent Assertions 8.x needs a paid licence, while open-source and non-commercial use stay free.
